t2.text: Pitcher page — controls without crowding the scene

s1.text: Homepage: the 3D scene becomes the hero (it IS the product). Copy speaks to front-office analysts and player-dev/coaches. Leaders move into a broadcast ticker + boards. No player headshots or club logos in the mock — swap the initials back for real headshots in code.

s2.text: CHOSEN. Option A — bottom sheet. Scene owns the top 60%. Active filters ride on the scene as removable chips; everything else lives in a draggable sheet with Arsenal / Filters / Games tabs. Arsenal rows double as the pitch-type filter (no duplicate control).

s3.text: NOT CHOSEN (reference only). Option B — toolbar + full-screen filters. Scene is full-bleed; one bottom toolbar. Filters open as a full page with a live pitch count on the apply button. Tap Filters in B1 to play the flow.

s4.text: Stats becomes a view toggle (3D scene | Stats) in the main area, not a rail tab — the rail keeps its job. Game line reads as a broadcast score bug; at-bat rows link straight into the replay. Per-pitch-type numbers, batter names and the at-bat sequence are SAMPLE values (the live APIs returned 401 from my sandbox) — wire to real data.

s5.text: Feature cards: hover (desktop) or tap (mobile) expands one card into a live preview + 3-step how-to + CTA into the real page. Paths animate in; reduced-motion shows them static. In production the preview should lazy-mount the real R3F scene only when the card opens.

s6.text: A was chosen and is applied to the homepage frames; B and C are reference only. Hero background options. A: your existing stadium-sunset photo behind a left-weighted scrim (copy stays legible). B: a lighter navy panel with faint field lines, strike-zone grid and dashed pitch arcs. C: a skewed broadcast slab behind the monitor with a crimson edge. The section below is dimmed for contrast.

s7.text: FOR THE CODING AGENT: read project/DESIGN.md first. It lists which frames to build vs ignore, all color/type tokens, interaction specs (feature-card expand, drawer, at-bat replay), and which numbers are sample data.
